input.quote: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
input.rationale: § 7.2 is a wrong-direction MFN: it binds Customer (Redwood) to give Vendor (Silverline) terms no less favourable than the best terms offered to any other technology supplier. This is open-ended (no defined product, no time limit, no comparison carve-outs), which sits at the playbook's walk-away position, and it directly contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Deleting § 7.2 is the minimal edit to reach the preferred position; no Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document that would be affected.

proposal.summary: Delete the Customer-side MFN obligation in § 7.2
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted § 7.2 because our playbook does not permit us to grant a most-favoured-nation commitment to Vendor, and an open-ended obligation to extend our best supplier terms is unworkable to administer. This also removes a direct conflict with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment; MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.
